official.deadline_note: Two deadlines matter in practice: the Master's programme application should realistically be submitted by 1 December 2026, because conditional admission must exist before the VUFP can be applied for, and the VUFP application itself closes 1 February 2027 (23:59 CET). Results are expected mid-March 2027 and offers must be accepted by end of March 2027.
official.application_cycle: 2027/2028: VUFP application opens 1 November 2026 and closes 1 February 2027, for Master's programmes starting September 2027
official.status_note: VU Amsterdam states 'Applications are welcome from November 1st 2026' with a deadline of 1 February 2027 (23:59 CET) for the intake starting September 2027; the Master's programme application opens 1 October 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: "The VUFP scholarship covers the tuition fees only. It does not provide any additional allowance towards study or living costs, like rent, food, insurances. Be aware that you must be able to finance these living expenses by yourself." VU Amsterdam has committed approximately 1 million euros to the programme as a whole.
benefits: Merit-based tuition fee waiver for the first year of a full-time English-taught Master's programme at VU Amsterdam
For a two-year programme the scholarship is extended only if 100% of the ECTS in the first year have been achieved
Applying for the VUFP automatically also applies for the NL Scholarship (formerly HSP), with no separate application
NL Scholarship: a one-time contribution of EUR 5,000 towards the costs of living for the entire study period, awarded only for the first year, with around 20-25 available per year
VUFP recipients act as an international student ambassador for the duration of their Master's studies
eligibility: You hold a non-EU/EEA passport and you are not eligible for the lower tuition fee, and you do not have the Dutch nationality
You can prove your academic excellence, with a GPA equivalent to a Dutch grade of 8.0, proven by the GPA proof or programme transcript plus a grading scale explanation
You are conditionally or unconditionally admitted to the first year of a full-time English-taught Master's programme starting September 2027

The degree with which you seek admission has not been obtained in the Netherlands, you have no degree from a Dutch institution, and you are not currently enrolled in a Bachelor or Master programme in the Netherlands
You do not need to complete a preparatory programme before the start of your Master
February starters cannot apply, and joint programmes where VU Amsterdam does not administer the admission process are excluded
Students already enrolled in a two-year Master's who were not awarded the VUFP in 2026/2027 are not eligible to apply for 2027/2028
requirements: Complete the VUFP-NLS application form (2027-2028 version; older versions will not be accepted) as one file in PDF format
Paste the GPA proof or programme transcript at the end of the form, together with a grading scale explanation, so the application counts as complete
You can apply for the VUFP for one Master's programme only, even if you applied for admission to more than one
You can submit your application only once and cannot resubmit
You must have been conditionally admitted to the Master's programme before applying for the VUFP
documents: Completed VUFP-NLS application form 2027-2028 as a single PDF, with all questions answered
GPA proof or programme transcript showing the most up-to-date grades, with a grading scale explanation
selection_criteria: Academic quality of the applicant, with the grade converted by the VUFP Scholarship Committee against the Dutch 8.0 equivalent using ECCTIS grade distribution data
Motivation for this university and the specific programme, future ambitions, and extracurricular activities, as recorded in the application form
Faculty nomination followed by decision of the Central VUFP / Central Scholarship Committee, in comparison with all other applicants
coverage: Tuition fees for the first year of the Master's programme (one- or two-year programmes, second year conditional on 100% of first-year ECTS)
No contribution to rent, food, insurance or other living costs
Separate and conditional: the NL Scholarship one-time EUR 5,000 contribution towards living costs, first year only, awarded to only a few VUFP awardees
application_method: Step 1: register for a Master's programme in Studielink from 1 October 2026 and complete it in your personal VU dashboard, advised deadline 1 December 2026
Step 2: wait for conditional admission, then submit the VUFP application from 1 November 2026 in the Scholarship section of your personal VU dashboard
Step 3: the Central VUFP Committee, with the faculty, decides who is offered a VUFP scholarship
Step 4: all applicants receive an email or notification with the decision, expected mid-March 2027
Step 5: selected candidates accept or decline in their personal VU dashboard by end of March 2027
official.application_route: Apply for admission to a Master's programme through Studielink and the VU dashboard first, obtain conditional admission, then submit the single-shot VUFP-NLS PDF application in the VU dashboard by 1 February 2027.
official.citizenship_residency: Non-EU/EEA passport, no Dutch nationality, no degree obtained in the Netherlands and no current enrolment in a Dutch Bachelor or Master programme
official.international_eligibility: Open to non-EU/EEA international students only; EU/EEA students pay the lower fee and are not eligible
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Any full-time English-taught Master's programme at VU Amsterdam, except February starts and joint programmes where VU Amsterdam does not administer admissions; the MBA faculty scholarships are separate schemes
official.duration: 1 or 2 years depending on the Master's programme, with the second year conditional on 100% of first-year ECTS
official.description: The VU Fellowship Programme (VUFP) offers talented prospective non-EU/EEA students the opportunity to pursue a Master's degree at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, funded from a commitment of approximately 1 million euros towards attracting highly motivated and excellent students. It is a merit-based tuition fee waiver and carries no living allowance.
official.program_type: Merit-based tuition fee waiver scholarship for incoming Master's students

not_confirmed: funding_amount, funding_currency, funding_period - VU Amsterdam publishes no euro value for the VUFP tuition waiver itself, only the approximately 1 million euro total programme commitment and the separate conditional NL Scholarship amount of EUR 5,000
english_requirement - the scholarship page sets no language certificate requirement of its own and defers to the admission requirements of the chosen programme
catalogue_url and official_updates_url - no dedicated pages were verified for this scholarship
verification.notes: All benefits, eligibility, deadlines, documents, procedure and selection criteria were read directly from VU Amsterdam's own scholarships page for incoming Master's students. The NL Scholarship is recorded as a separate conditional award because only a few of the VUFP awardees receive it.

applicant_utility.summary: Treat admission and the scholarship as one continuous race: you cannot even open the VUFP form until VU has conditionally admitted you, so a Master's application left past early December turns a February scholarship deadline into something you cannot realistically meet. The application is a single-submission affair - one form, one programme, no second chance - so the PDF must be complete, with the GPA proof and grading scale pasted in, before you click submit. Because the committee converts your grades against the Dutch 8.0 using grade distribution data rather than a fixed conversion table, a mid-range GPA from a country with generous marking may still clear the bar while a raw percentage alone tells you little.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong non-EU/EEA applicants with a graded bachelor's transcript from outside the Netherlands and a clear reason for choosing one specific VU Master's programme, who can secure conditional admission by early December.
application_readiness_checklist: Start the Studielink and VU dashboard Master's application by mid-November 2026 so conditional admission arrives before the VUFP window is consumed
Produce a transcript or GPA proof showing the grading scale and an explanation of how your GPA was calculated, since an unexplained score makes the application incomplete
Decide which single Master's programme you will name on the VUFP form before applying for admission elsewhere, and write the motivation around that programme specifically
Download the 2027-2028 VUFP-NLS form from the VU page rather than reusing an older version, and merge everything into one PDF
Diarise the acceptance deadline of end of March 2027 alongside your visa and housing planning, because an unanswered offer is withdrawn after two weeks
common_rejection_risks: Applying for admission to several Master's programmes and then discovering you may only name one on the VUFP form
Submitting an application missing any question or the GPA proof or grading scale, which VU states will not be evaluated at all
Assuming conditional admission will be in place in time when the programme's own application or intake assessment runs longer than advertised
Missing that February starters, joint programmes VU does not administer, and applicants who already hold a Dutch degree are excluded
Reapplying after a failed 2026/2027 bid while already enrolled in a two-year programme, which the rules bar explicitly
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Rent, food, insurance and all other living costs in Amsterdam are not covered by the VUFP; only the small number of awardees who also receive the NL Scholarship get a one-time EUR 5,000 towards living, and only for the first year. Tuition must still be paid before 31 August or you are not enrolled and cannot start.
document_audit: The application form must be one PDF file, so combine form, transcript and grading scale before uploading rather than attaching separate files
Only your bachelor's GPA is assessed, even if you already hold a Master's degree, so do not build the case around later qualifications
If you have not yet graduated, the most up-to-date transcript is what counts, so obtain it close to the application date
Keep the emailed evidence of conditional admission, since the VUFP application depends on it
Scores sent by email ahead of the application period are not assessed, so nothing outside the formal submission will be looked at
alerts: The one-submission rule is absolute: VU states you will not be allowed to submit again, so treat the first submission as final
A VUFP award cannot be postponed to another academic year if your plans change
If you are not awarded the VUFP you are also not awarded the NL Scholarship, since the two are linked in one application
VUFP recipients take on an international student ambassador role for the whole Master's, including Unibuddy enquiries from prospective students
Second-year funding for a two-year programme requires 100% of first-year ECTS, so a single failed course can end the award
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Admission first through Studielink and the VU dashboard until conditional admission arrives, then a one-off PDF upload in the Scholarship section of the VU dashboard by 1 February 2027, faculty review, Central Committee decision, email result in mid-March 2027, and acceptance in the dashboard by end of March 2027.
